AdjacencyPredicate.description:
What the geometry touches.

An edge between a flat face and a cylinder is the rim of a hole, and says
so without knowing where the hole is.
AdjacencyPredicate.title: AdjacencyPredicate

ArcSegment.description:
An arc given by its two endpoints, its centre and a direction.

Endpoints and centre over centre-radius-angles because it is the form that
makes a contour verifiable: the previous segment's end has to equal this
segment's start, and with angles that is an inference rather than a
comparison. The adapter converts to what KOMPAS wants.

`sweep` is not redundant with the endpoints: two arcs share every endpoint
and centre and differ only in which way round they go.
ArcSegment.title: ArcSegment

ConstraintKind.description:
Every constraint KOMPAS v22 was measured to support.

Named after what they mean rather than after the integers KOMPAS uses. The
integers were identified by measurement — the type libraries export no
enumerations at all — and live in the adapter, next to the COM call they
belong to.
ConstraintKind.title: ConstraintKind

DatumPlaneOffsetFeature.description:
An auxiliary plane, so a later sketch has somewhere to sit.

A feature rather than a `reference_geometry` entry because it depends on
other features and other features depend on it, and the dependency graph is
the one place that is already stated and checked.
DatumPlaneOffsetFeature.title: DatumPlaneOffsetFeature

DatumPlaneOffsetInputs.description:
An auxiliary plane parallel to another, a stated distance away.

Offset only. A plane at an angle or through three points is expressible in
KOMPAS and will be added when something needs one; adding it now would mean
three build paths with one test each.
DatumPlaneOffsetInputs.title: DatumPlaneOffsetInputs

DimensionKind.description:
The dimension kinds KOMPAS was measured to bind to a named variable.

Angular is absent deliberately: `IAngleDimensions.Add` answers with nothing
for every type tried, so an angular dimension cannot yet be created at all.
Recorded in docs/TASK-POSTMVP-007-sketch-constraints.md rather than guessed
at here.
DimensionKind.title: DimensionKind

DocumentMetadata.description:
Who wrote this document, not which model wrote it.

Model, reasoning effort and CLI version belong to the AI run that produced
the document (ADR-017). Putting them here would change the canonical hash
of an identical part whenever the model changed, which would make the hash
useless for the one thing it is for.
DocumentMetadata.title: DocumentMetadata

DrivingDimension.description:
A named measurement of the sketch, stated and then verified.

The `id` is the stable name the roadmap asks for — `base_width`,
`hole_pitch_x`, `wall_thickness` — and it becomes the variable's name in the
KOMPAS model, so the same word appears in the document, in the delivered
file and in any later diff.

`value` is what the document says the measurement is. The adapter reads what
KOMPAS measured and refuses the difference: a dimension that disagrees with
the geometry it dimensions is a document contradicting itself.
DrivingDimension.title: DrivingDimension

ExactlyN.description:
A count the document states rather than discovers.

`exactly_n` is how a pattern says "these four mounting holes". If the model
grows a fifth, the mismatch is the point: the document no longer describes
the part.
ExactlyN.title: ExactlyN

FeatureResult.description:
Something a feature creates that a later feature may refer to.

Naming results explicitly is what lets a later operation say "the body the
base extrusion made" instead of "whatever the previous feature left
behind", which stops meaning the same thing as soon as features are
reordered.
FeatureResult.title: FeatureResult

Measurement.description:
A measured quantity with the tolerance it must be matched within.

The tolerance is required. Comparing floating-point geometry for equality
is a bug waiting for a rebuild, and letting it default hides the choice
from whoever later wonders why a face stopped matching.
Measurement.title: Measurement

ParameterRef.description: A reference to a named parameter, the only indirection CAD-IR allows.
ParameterRef.title: ParameterRef

PathContour.description:
A closed boundary spelled out segment by segment.

The general form. Everything else in this module is a shape that expands
into one of these deterministically.
PathContour.title: PathContour

SketchConstraint.description:
One statement about the sketch that must already be true.

`of` and `to` name entities by their sketch-local ids, never by position in
a list. A constraint on "segment 2" would change meaning when segments are
reordered, which is the index problem ADR-019 exists to prevent, one level
down.
SketchConstraint.title: SketchConstraint

SketchOnDatumPlane.description: A sketch on an auxiliary plane some earlier feature produced.
SketchOnDatumPlane.title: SketchOnDatumPlane

SketchOnFace.description:
A sketch on a face of the model, named by what the face means.

The selector is resolved at build time against the model as it then is. The
document never records which face was chosen, because a face index stops
meaning the same thing after the next rebuild — the whole argument of
ADR-019.
SketchOnFace.title: SketchOnFace

SketchPoint.description:
Which point of an entity a point constraint is about.

Naming it is not optional. In a closed contour consecutive segments meet
end-to-start, so a coincidence that always meant "start to start" would be
false for every corner of every rectangle.
SketchPoint.title: SketchPoint

SlotContour.description: A straight slot: two end-cap centres and the radius that rounds them.
SlotContour.title: SlotContour

SourceRegion.description:
Where on the drawing a value came from, in normalised page coordinates.

Optional, and kept out of the geometry: it exists so a wrong dimension can
be traced back to the mark that produced it.
SourceRegion.title: SourceRegion

Sweep.description: Which way round an arc goes from its start point to its end point.
Sweep.title: Sweep
